previous_abstract:
\abstract{
\Euclid\ measures weak-lensing shapes with VIS at $0\farcs1$ sampling,
while its near-infrared imager NISP detects red and high-redshift
galaxies that VIS cannot measure, but at $0\farcs3$ sampling too coarse
for shapes. Super-resolving NISP imaging could extend weak lensing into
the near-infrared, raising the effective source density and the
redshift reach of the lensing sample. Like any shape-measurement
technique, however, a learned method's biases must be quantified before
its outputs can inform cosmology. Here we evaluate image fidelity and
observed-shape agreement for deep-learning super-resolution of NISP imaging. We
train a conditional diffusion model and two residual-network variants on
17\,816 NISP \YE-band cutouts of the COSMOS field paired with JWST/NIRCam
F115W imaging at five times finer sampling.
Diffusion learns a generative prior, while the residual networks learn
direct mappings.
On 2118 validation galaxies, the residual models have lower source-region
reconstruction errors and stronger signed Fourier correlation with the
JWST reference, while diffusion retains more observed small-scale power.
ResNet reconstruction errors are consistent across three independent
training seeds.
Observed-shape error reductions are largest in the highest input signal-to-noise bin.
A controlled simulation with supplied NISP effective PSFs finds greater shear response for the ResNet than for native NISP in the two displayed compact-galaxy cases, but not uniformly over the full size and noise grid.
These validation diagnostics include noise, instrumental responses, and
the band difference, and do not establish calibrated shear recovery.
The 2876-object test sample remains reserved for evaluation of the fixed
model and measurement choices.
    }
new_abstract:
\abstract{
\Euclid's near-infrared NISP imaging offers access to galaxy populations relevant to weak lensing, but its coarse sampling limits measurements of galaxy structure.
We investigate whether learned super-resolution improves image fidelity and observed shapes while preserving sensitivity to applied shear.
We train a conditional diffusion model and two residual-network variants on 17\,816 NISP \YE-band cutouts paired with JWST/NIRCam F115W images, and evaluate them on 2118 validation galaxies.
Residual networks achieve lower reconstruction errors and stronger spatial correlation with JWST than diffusion, whereas diffusion retains more observed small-scale power.
Relative to native NISP, ResNet reduces ellipticity-component RMSE by approximately 19\% with fixed weighted moments and 11\% with adaptive moments on matched successful samples.
Improvements are largest at high signal-to-noise; low-signal comparisons are limited by measurement selection.
Reconstruction errors are consistent across three training seeds.
Controlled simulations using supplied NISP effective point-spread functions show increased ResNet shear response for compact galaxies, but gains depend on size and noise, and responses remain below intrinsic values.
These results support residual networks as a promising approach to improving observed-shape fidelity in NISP imaging and motivate further investigation for weak lensing.
Establishing calibrated shear accuracy will require realistic simulations and independent validation that account for noise, instrumental response, cross-band differences, and measurement selection.
}
